findings.summary: _end_active_session atexit handler unconditionally ends the session, ignoring the skip_auto_end_session config option (env AGENTOPS_SKIP_AUTO_END_SESSION) which documents 'Whether to skip automatically ending sessions on program exit'
findings.failure_scenario: User sets skip_auto_end_session=True or AGENTOPS_SKIP_AUTO_END_SESSION=true, expecting managed session lifecycle; process exits, _end_active_session fires anyway, prematurely ending and flushing the session span

findings.summary: Omitting context parameter on tracer.start_span() for SESSION spans does NOT create a root span; OpenTelemetry's Tracer.start_span() defaults context=None to context_api.get_current() internally, matching old behavior exactly
findings.failure_scenario: An agent span is active when start_session() is called; the session span's start_span() internally resolves to get_current() and parents under the agent span instead of becoming a root, breaking the intended trace hierarchy

findings.summary: Module-level _atexit_registered flag is never reset; after os.fork(), child processes inherit the flag as True but atexit handlers don't survive fork, so no handler is registered and child sessions leak unreported
findings.failure_scenario: Parent process initializes AgentOps; multiprocessing fork creates worker; worker calls start_session() but atexit registration is skipped; worker exits without ending the session; span data is lost

findings.summary: Setting _active_session in start_session() is wrapped in try/except that passes silently; if the import or assignment fails, _current_session is set but _active_session is not, so the atexit handler has no reference to end the session
findings.failure_scenario: import agentops.client.client raises unexpectedly inside start_session; _active_session stays None/None; _current_session is set to a valid session; process exits; _end_active_session handler sees _active_session is None and does nothing; session span leaks

findings.summary: Error recovery fallback in end_session() calls span.end() directly instead of _finalize_span(), skipping context token detach and tracer_provider.force_flush()
findings.failure_scenario: _set_span_attributes succeeds but _finalize_span raises (e.g., broken connection); fallback ends the span directly; context_api.detach(token) is never called, leaking the context token for the thread's lifetime; spans already buffered are not force-flushed

findings.summary: _finalize_span() internally calls tracer_provider.force_flush(), yet _flush_span_processors() (which also calls force_flush()) is still invoked immediately after, causing a redundant double flush on every session end
findings.failure_scenario: Every end_session call triggers two force_flush() calls on the tracer provider; doubled network I/O during session teardown with no benefit

findings.summary: context_api.get_current() is called and its return value discarded; in the OpenTelemetry Python SDK this has no observable side effect (the context module is already initialized at import time)
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime impact; the call is dead code that confuses readers expecting it to initialize something
